talks.title: Ai, Deception And Deepfakes When Trust Becomes The Primary Attack Surface
talks.teaser: Engineers explore architecture and security mechanisms for Ai, Deception And Deepfakes When Trust Becomes The Primary Attack Surface.
talks.summary:
Overview: A nullcon panel explores AI, deception, and deepfakes as emerging attack surfaces where trust itself becomes the primary vulnerability across fintech, insurance, transport, and national security sectors.

Key Topics: Deepfake-enabled fraud in regulated sectors; North Korean synthetic identity infiltration of US companies and universities; trust erosion in hiring and authentication; and balancing AI defensive capabilities against offensive deception campaigns.

Technical Details: Panelists discuss how AI-generated synthetic identities undermine background checks and hiring pipelines. The fintech representative highlights critical infrastructure implications while the ex-military panelist frames threats from a national security perspective.

Takeaways: Deepfakes attack the trust layer underlying business operations and national security. Organizations in regulated sectors need multi-factor identity verification beyond document checks and video interviews.

talks.title: Cloud Resilience Simplified Less Data, Stronger Security
talks.teaser: Industry experts analyze emerging threats surrounding Cloud Resilience Simplified Less Data, Stronger Security.
talks.summary:
Cloud Resilience Framing

A nullcon panel explores cloud resilience through data minimization and simplified architecture. Moderators argue that reducing data volume shrinks attack surface, speeds recovery, and strengthens security—linking India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act to resilience rather than compliance alone.

Discovering Dark Data

Panelists define dark data as unclassified, uncorrelated information in blind spots—obsolete OneDrive files, forgotten test databases, and decommissioned microservice data without lifecycle plans. Discovery requires cataloging structured versus unstructured data and applying classification tags.

Developer and Security Practices

Recommendations include data minimization at collection, assigning data ownership accountability, and embedding legal-retention hooks in code. DLP solutions protect classified data, while architects must plan data lifecycle when modernizing to microservices.

Attacker Entry Points

From an offensive perspective, orphaned and shadow data often becomes the weakest link—not always directly internet-exposed but reachable through application or perimeter vulnerabilities, making forgotten datasets high-value targets.

talks.title: Demystifying Driver Research A Systematic Approach For Vulnerability Hunting
talks.teaser: Industry experts analyze emerging threats surrounding Demystifying Driver Research A Systematic Approach For Vulnerability Hunting.
talks.summary:
Why Drivers Matter

Priyanu presents at Nullcon on hunting vulnerabilities in signed Windows kernel drivers whose IOCTL interfaces let user-mode code reach privileged operations—valuable for red teams disabling EDR and for defenders prioritizing risky drivers.

Beyond Random Fuzzing

He calls out the beginner fallacy of fuzzing every driver blindly. Most drivers are poor targets; a repeatable pipeline beats one-off luck, and he cites his first CVE and professional engagement using this approach.

Five-Step Pipeline

The workflow starts with mass driver collection from DriverPack, Internet Archive, and cabinet extraction tools. API import filtering finds IoCreateDevice and IoCreateSymbolicLink usage, then dynamic loading verifies a user-reachable device actually appears.

Manual Review

Filtered drivers undergo reverse engineering: inspect dispatch tables, follow IRP_MJ_DEVICE_CONTROL handlers, and hunt memory corruption bugs. Exploit development is out of scope; the goal is consistent zero-day discovery rather than isolated fuzz hits.

talks.title: Dpdpa In Action Designing A 72 Hour Breach Response That Actually Works
talks.teaser: Industry experts analyze emerging threats surrounding Dpdpa In Action Designing A 72 Hour Breach Response That Actually Works.
talks.summary:
Regulatory focus

A Nullcon panel examines India's DPDP Act Section 8 and Rule 7, requiring data fiduciaries to notify data principals and the Data Protection Board when a personal-data breach occurs.

Cyber vs privacy incidents

INOX GFL group CISO contrasts triggers: ransomware/extortion calls versus media/public leak discovery. Core assets differ (infrastructure vs personal data), impacts differ (ransom vs penalties up to hundreds of crores), and owners differ (CISO vs DPO), though roles often overlap.

Reporting lens

Cyber incidents may fall under IT Act timelines; privacy incidents invoke DPDP/GDPR-style regimes with 72-hour notification expectations.

Proactive response

JSW Paints' Neelamani Sahu urges internal breach identification before public exposure, board notification, then principal communication in plain language covering what leaked, mitigation steps, and user actions. Public discovery means failed controls and reactive damage control rather than ideal playbook execution.

talks.title: Regulation, Resilience and Reality: How CXOs Navigate the Compliance Security Trade-Off
talks.teaser: Presenters detail vulnerability discovery and exploitation in Regulation, Resilience and Reality: How CXOs Navigate the Compliance Security Trade-Off.
talks.summary:
## Overview
A Nullcon CXO panel deliberately avoids scripted GPT-style answers, debating how executives balance regulation, resilience, and operational reality.

## Three Lines of Defense
Panelists frame security governance as business ownership (first line), risk and resilience practices (second), and audit (third). Several argue audit-at-the-end is too late in the AI transformation era—controls must shift into design and build phases.

## Human and Organizational Factors
Clear accountability across the business matters more than checkbox compliance. Burnout on security teams is itself a cyber risk. During incidents, fast, factual, honest communication can make or break response.

## Future Outlook
AI will reshape both offense and defense—automated phishing, deepfakes, and nation-state activity are accelerating. The panel urges merging assurance lines rather than treating compliance as a terminal gate.
